solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prisoner taking bait showing disrespect

parts.note: a con is crossword shorthand for a convict, a prisoner
to bait is to lure or entice, to tempt

explanation.surface: A jailbird who rises to the bait is showing contempt for the guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrespect and scorn are close synonyms for the same disdainful attitude.

clue.text: Girl touring Chilean capital, memorable

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the girl's name encloses a letter

parts.note: Cathy is a girl's name

indicators.note: capital here means the first, capital letter of Chilean

explanation.surface: A girl's tour of Santiago was memorable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilean capital' wants to be Santiago; it is just C.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that is easily remembered is said to be catchy.

clue.text: National alpine resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again

explanation.surface: A national ski resort in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but means sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country; this is a citizen of the Himalayan kingdom.

clue.text: A person upset, I hate that! Stop it!

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: one can mean a person, as in one does
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone upset crying that they hate something and want it to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying that's sufficient is a way of telling someone to stop.

clue.text: Gather a flower, say, for East Indian food

indicators.note: say signals the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to pick a lily is to gather a flower

explanation.surface: Picking a flower, perhaps for an Indian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustard and vegetable pickle of East Indian origin, eaten as a relish.

clue.text: Number of horses on solid ground

definitions.meaning: a racing yard's set of horses kept by one trainer
firm, secure, not liable to give way

explanation.surface: A string of racehorses kept on firm footing.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a trainer's collection of horses, and an adjective for something firmly fixed and steady.

clue.text: Principally, outrageous cuts finished comprehensive

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the word for finished

parts.note: through can mean finished, as in I'm through

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, taking the first letter of outrageous

explanation.surface: Mainly outrageous cuts completed a comprehensive programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done exhaustively, leaving nothing out, is comprehensive.

clue.text: Drunk back late — it's the drink

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drank too much and came back late, blaming a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea served without milk is a drink.

clue.text: Writer in Cervantes, say, is talismanic

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A writer such as Cervantes has magical power.
explanation.walkthrough: Cervantes, a novelist, looks like the definition's example, but he only hides the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of short prose pieces on a subject is a kind of writer.

clue.text: Excellent work with recollection of hundred bagged by test cricket's hardworking openers

indicators.note: being bagged by something is being put inside it, so the opening letters enclose the rest
openers are the first letters of the words test, cricket's and hardworking

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: re-collection read cryptically as collecting backwards, so the word for hundred is turned round

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred, e.g. a century in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator praising a century scored by a test side's industrious opening batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollection' is read as re-collection, collecting backwards, which is why it signals a turnaround; a ton is a cricket century.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate and excellent are synonyms for the highest quality.

clue.text: Other ranks in service giving ground

indicators.note: the ranks letters sit inside the church service

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Enlisted soldiers on duty losing territory in a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or marsh is soft, wet ground where one gets stuck.

clue.text: Stand-out image in amateur boxing record, gold-plated

indicators.note: boxing something is putting it in a box, enclosing it

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, especially a radio enthusiast or poor actor

indicators.note: gold-plated reads as the record coated by gold, so the gold letters wrap round it

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a log is a written record, such as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A souvenir photograph of a gold medal won by an amateur boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'gold-plated' does two jobs: 'gold' gives the letters and 'plated' says they coat the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-dimensional laser picture seems to stand out from its surface, hence a stand-out image.

clue.text: Humorous trousers beginning to chafe for hurdler, perhaps?

indicators.note: used as a verb: to trouser is to pocket, so the word for humorous takes in a letter

parts.note: jokey means full of jokes, humorous

indicators.note: the beginning of chafe is its first letter

explanation.surface: Comic trousers starting to rub a hurdler's legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb here, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider in steeplechases or hurdle races could be called a hurdler, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Retailer has a job bagging satin pants

indicators.note: bagging means putting in a bag, so the job word encloses the rest

parts.note: a chore is a job, a routine task

indicators.note: pants as British slang means rubbish, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A shop worker's job is bagging up satin underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' as British slang means rubbish, so it signals SATIN rearranged into AINST.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer with many branches selling the same goods.

clue.text: Fashionable bears in trousers

parts.note: hip means trendy, fashionable
bears are thought of as squeezing people, the origin of the bear hug, so bears are cuddlers

explanation.surface: Trendy teddy bears dressed in trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-rise trousers that sit tightly on the hips rather than the waist are a kind of trousers.

clue.text: Non-English promoted sides financially fail supporter

indicators.note: in a down clue promoted means moved up, read upwards
the word must lose its E for English

parts.note: faces are the sides of a solid shape
a business that folds goes under financially

explanation.surface: Football talk: foreign-led promoted teams going bust lets a fan down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-English' takes E out of FACES to give FACS, and 'promoted' turns that upwards into SCAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders' scaffolding is a framework that supports workers and structures.

clue.text: A suit held up by Japanese staple, clever trick

indicators.note: the staple food holds the turned word inside it

parts.note: rice is the staple food of Japan

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards

parts.note: to suit is to fit

explanation.surface: A business suit held up by a staple from Japan, a clever trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staple' is not a fastener but a basic food; 'up' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Artful cunning or a crafty ruse is a clever trick.

clue.text: Still popular, concert leader in uplifting musical

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the leader goes inside the musical's letters
in a down clue uplifting means read upwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: the leader of concert is its first letter

explanation.surface: A conductor still popular in a feelgood musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns EVITA into ATIVE, and C, the concert 'leader', goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being still means not moving, idle and motionless.

clue.text: Orchestra member rarely is after a drink (sounded drunk)

indicators.note: is comes after the drink in the answer
something drunk is swallowed, so the drink takes in the word for sounded

parts.note: cola is a fizzy drink
rang means sounded, as a bell does

explanation.surface: An orchestral player who seldom drinks sounds tipsy when they do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like an anagram signal but means swallowed by the drink. 'rarely' plays no part in the wordplay; the blog suggests it hints that the instrument is an uncommon member.
explanation.definitionFit: The English horn, a tenor oboe, is a woodwind instrument played in orchestras.

clue.text: Newspaper copy

definitions.meaning: a British tabloid daily of that name

explanation.surface: A newspaper copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A British tabloid paper's title, and a verb for imitating or reflecting something exactly.

clue.text: Toy instrument

definitions.meaning: to toy is to play idly with something

explanation.surface: A toy musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for fidgeting idly with something, and the informal name for a violin.

clue.text: Settled on old houses

indicators.note: the old word houses, holds, the other letters

parts.note: aged means old
re means on or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: Elderly people settled into old houses.
explanation.definitionFit: When a matter is settled, all parties have consented to it.

clue.text: Bird circling lake, quail

indicators.note: the bird goes round the lake's letter

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bird flying round a lake, alongside a quail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quail' is not another bird but the verb to cower.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, the same as to recoil or wince.

clue.text: A resilience about one being hopeful

indicators.note: the springiness word goes about, round, the numeral one

parts.note: spring means bounce or elasticity, resilience
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bouncy personality makes someone hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ambitious who aims for success is hopeful of it.

clue.text: Foundation taking payment back in

indicators.note: back means the payment word is read backwards

parts.note: a giro is a British bank transfer or state benefit payment

explanation.surface: An organisation founded by bringing in payments.
explanation.walkthrough: A giro is a British state benefit payment or bank transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A source or starting point is the foundation from which something grows.

clue.text: Cooler time for hot breakfast?

definitions.meaning: a cooler is slang for prison, and doing time there is British slang for a stretch inside
a hot oat dish eaten in the morning

explanation.surface: Looks like a choice between something chilled and something warm in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' and 'hot' look like opposites of temperature; cooler is slang for jail. The word as British slang for a prison sentence is well known from a 1970s sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a prison sentence, and the oatmeal dish eaten warm at breakfast.

clue.text: Some concrete ideas rejected, as fat loser

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
some of the words concrete ideas supply a run of letters

explanation.surface: Some solid plans were turned down, a reference to weight-loss schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks RETEID from concrETE IDeas, and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a slimming regime is trying to lose fat, hence a fat loser.

clue.text: Help to turn around end of tiresome day

indicators.note: the turning word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to bend is to turn or curve

indicators.note: end of tiresome is its last letter

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday

explanation.surface: Someone asking for help to get through the end of a tiring day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' looks like part of the definition 'Help to', but it is the wordplay's bending word.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a friend to someone is to help and support them.
